memory_update.text: LHX is the clearest public-market munitions/propulsion capacity candidate because Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motor assets map directly to missile-defense and long-range-fires expansion.

HII is a direct shipyard-capacity candidate for the FY2026 shipbuilding and maritime industrial-base theme, but margin and execution risk must be tracked closely because GAO continues to flag Navy shipbuilding delays and cost overruns.
BWXT is a high-certification regulated-input candidate for Columbia/Virginia/Ford naval nuclear propulsion programs, with unusually direct evidence from announced reactor-component contracts.
CW should be tracked as a second-order qualified component supplier across naval, defense electronics, and nuclear-related markets; program-level mapping remains the main evidence gap.

CRS adds materials-layer exposure: specialty alloys for defense, missiles, marine systems, and aerospace. It may benefit if casting/forging and specialty-metal capacity becomes a policy-funded bottleneck.

Cyber/government IT and space-sensor/software suppliers were not prioritized in this 5-name pass because the search focus emphasized scarce suppliers, equipment, materials, components, infrastructure providers, regulated inputs, and capacity constraints. Future passes should examine CACI, SAIC, BAH, LDOS, PLTR, MRCY, RTX, LMT, NOC, RKLB, and selected space payload/sensor vendors.
